title: Ethiopian Brown Lentil Stew
localName: ቡናማ ምስር ወጥ — Bunama Misir Wat
community: All of Ethiopia — the whole lentil fasting stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Brown Lentil Stew — whole brown lentils simmered in a berbere sauce. Unlike red lentils which dissolve, brown lentils retain their shape — producing a chunkier, more textured stew. A satisfying variety change from Misir Wat.
longDesc: Brown lentil stew uses whole lentils where Misir Wat uses red (split) lentils — the result is more textured, requiring longer cooking but providing a different and equally satisfying eating experience.
ingredients: 2 cups brown or green lentils — washed, soaked 1 hour
steps: Add oil and berbere. Fry 3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add drained lentils. Stir to coat.
Brown lentils hold their shape — they will not dissolve like red lentils.
chefTips: Brown lentils need soaking — reduces cooking time.
They retain their shape — not as smooth as Misir Wat.
commonMistakes: Expecting red-lentil-style dissolving — brown lentils stay whole.
cookingScience: Brown lentils have their seed coat intact — this coat prevents the rapid water absorption and dissolution of red (dehulled) lentils. The seed coat proteins are also more resistant to heat denaturation, maintaining structural integrity through cooking.
sustainabilityTips: Brown lentils — the most common lentil globally, widely available.
servedWith: On the fasting platter as variety from Misir Wat
culturalNote: Brown lentil stew provides texture variety on the Ethiopian fasting platter — its chunky character a pleasant contrast to the smooth Misir Wat and silky Shiro.
